flags: ODOT cache/01.txt is truncated mid-record and contains no Marys Peak byway entry. Cannot independently establish catalog ODOT attributes or formal state-designation date from it. Travel Oregon establishes the named scenic byway and both spurs.
Travel Oregon gives 72 miles, while catalog mapped distance is 98.2; scope of spur mileage is not explained. Used the tourism drive description without claiming it includes all spur travel.
Strip miles run coast-to-inland; prose and retained moments run inland-to-coast, matching Travel Oregon and current story. All retained titles and coordinates preserved.

Dropped the current implication that the whole route descends from the Coast Range summit: the peak is a spur, not the starting point. Also restored the clear-day condition to eastward summit views, which current text left unqualified. Other current narrative facts are supported; Tangent etymology and Waldport naming were omitted for focus.

Current winter advice is present in the Marys Peak secondary article but tied to a 2010–2011 Forest Service announcement; no current road-manager page verifies it. Omitted open-road and equipment guarantees, and did not extend Travel Oregon’s year-round description to summit access.
The cache has no main-highway construction narrative; history uses documented spur construction and a corridor bridge. Alsea Falls moment is short because its cached descriptive evidence is limited.
Marys Peak elevation is 4,097 feet in Travel Oregon and the Coast Range prose, but 4,101 in that article’s peak list. Used the tourism figure; datum difference is unresolved.
Current story and moments have no motifs fields; supplied an empty story motifs array and preserved absent moment motifs.
